title: Recipe
description: Curated knowledge about how a sound is built: which gear a player or style uses, and how it should behave. A Recipe is an input to preset generation; a RigSpec is the output. A Recipe names real-world gear ("Ampeg SVT") and never a device model identifier, so one Recipe serves every Helix device and survives Line 6 renaming a model.

id.description: Stable identifier, matching the filename stem.

kind.description: Whether this describes a named player or a style with no particular player in mind.

name.description: How a person would refer to this, e.g. "Mike Dirnt".

band.description: The act the player is best known for. Helps disambiguate a request.

instrument_type.description: Selects which half of the device catalog is eligible. Line 6 tags every amp and cab Guitar or Bass.

aliases.description: Other ways a person might ask for this, matched case-insensitively.

variants.description: Per-song or per-era departures. Settings move; gear does not.

rig.description: The stable layer. Career-long for an artist, definitional for a genre. A wrong amp here is a bad miss; a wrong value in `character` is a near miss.

instrument.description: The guitar or bass itself, e.g. "Fender Precision Bass". Not modelled by the device, but it informs pickup character and output level.

amp.description: Real-world amplifier, e.g. "Ampeg SVT". Resolved through schemas/gear-map.json.

cab.description: Real-world speaker cabinet, e.g. "Ampeg 8x10". Omit to accept the amp's default pairing, which Line 6 states as `cablink`.

pedals.description: Real-world pedals in signal order, e.g. ["Klon Centaur"]. Empty means none, which is a claim; omit the field if unknown.

technique.description: How the instrument is played, where it changes the sound — "pick, near the bridge", "fingerstyle", "palm muted".

character.description: How it should sound, in the words a person would use — "mid-forward, not scooped", "grit only on hard attack". The generator turns these into parameter moves against the catalog's real ranges. Prefer describing the result over naming a control.

technique.description: Overrides the rig's technique for this variant only.

provenance.description: Where this came from and how much to trust it. Not decoration: `llm` means a model asserted it and nobody checked, which is reliable for well-known players and unreliable for obscure ones — and the model cannot always tell which it is doing.

source.description: `llm` asserted by a model, unverified. `curated` confirmed by a person. `cited` traceable to a named source. Curated and cited outrank llm.

notes.description: What specifically is uncertain, so a reader knows what to check first.
